paper_metadata.title: A quantum spectral method for simulating stochastic processes, with applications to Monte Carlo

summary: This paper presents gate-based quantum spectral simulation methods for stochastic processes, including Brownian motion with resource bounds O(L + polylog(T)) gates, O(L + log T) qubits, and L = O(1/epsilon), and fractional Brownian motion with L = O(1/epsilon^(1/2H)). It also gives a coherent-encoding quantum Monte Carlo method with gate complexity eO(polylog(T)/epsilon^(1+1/2H)) and classical comparison O(T/epsilon^2), but all results are theoretical and no hardware experiment is reported.

experiments.description: Quantum algorithm for generating approximate analog encodings of Brownian motion trajectories using a truncated Wiener series, Gaussian state loading, and the discrete sine transform.

algorithm.variant: Quantum spectral simulation of Brownian motion via truncated Wiener series and QFT/DST

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Trajectory values are encoded in amplitudes over a time register; Fourier coefficients are loaded as amplitudes with decay 1/k, then transformed by the discrete sine transform.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare an ϵ-approximate analog encoding of a Brownian bridge / Brownian motion trajectory over T time steps.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation of the Wiener series to L terms; no penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Brownian motion / Brownian bridge simulation on T time steps.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate Wiener series; use Gaussian coefficients with variance decay 1/k; apply DST.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classically compute/prepare truncated Gaussian coefficients and data-loader angles.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial / polylog(T) vs O(T log T)
speedup_claims.conditions: when T ≫ L and L is chosen as O(1/ϵ)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this is a theoretical algorithmic result; no hardware experiment is reported.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; asymptotic speedup only. Quantum cost O(L + polylog(T)) vs classical O(T log T).
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: O(L + log T) qubits, eO(log L + log T) depth, O(L + polylog(T)) gates with L = O(1/epsilon).
limiting_factors: Requires coherent state preparation and QFT/DST
Speedup depends on truncation parameter L
Classical preprocessing of Gaussian coefficients and angles remains

notes: No hardware experiment is reported; this is a theoretical algorithmic result.
Resource bounds are stated in Theorem 4.1 and surrounding text.
The paper reports an asymptotic algorithmic improvement over classical O(T log T), but no experiment or device-level benchmark.

experiments.description: Quantum algorithm for generating approximate analog encodings of fractional Brownian motion trajectories for arbitrary Hurst parameter H.

algorithm.variant: Quantum spectral simulation of fractional Brownian motion via truncated Fourier series

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Fourier coefficients decay as k^-(H+0.5); the state is prepared with amplitudes proportional to 1/k^(H+0.5) and transformed to the time domain.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare an ϵ-approximate analog encoding of fractional Brownian motion trajectories.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation to L terms; no penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Fractional Brownian motion simulation for arbitrary Hurst parameter H.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use truncated stochastic Fourier series with power-law decay determined by H.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical truncation and coefficient scaling based on H.

classical_baselines.method_name: classical FFT-based fractional Brownian motion simulation

speedup_claims.factor: polylog(T) vs O(T log T), with improved dependence on ϵ for H > 1/2
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical FFT-based fractional Brownian motion simulation
speedup_claims.conditions: for H in (0,1], especially H > 1/2 where fewer terms are needed
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes the result is theoretical and that the exact number of terms depends on H.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: O(L + log T) qubits, eO(log L + log T) depth, O(L + polylog(T)) gates with L = O(1/epsilon^(1/2H)).
limiting_factors: Truncation cost grows as H decreases

notes: No hardware experiment is reported; this is a theoretical algorithmic result.
Resource bounds are stated in Theorem 4.11 and surrounding text.

experiments.description: Quantum spectral method for preparing amplitude encodings of stochastic integrals over Lévy processes using circulant embedding and the QFT.

algorithm.variant: Quantum spectral method for stochastic integrals via circulant embedding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Kernel vector is embedded into a circulant matrix; QFT diagonalizes the circulant operator to implement the stochastic integral.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare an amplitude encoding of F(t)=∫_0^t K(s,t)dμ_s.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Postselection in the diagonal-multiplication step; truncation to L Fourier coefficients.

problem_instance.description: Stochastic integral simulation for Lévy noise and Brownian-motion special case.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute Fourier coefficients of the noise, truncate to L terms, and embed Toeplitz matrix into a circulant matrix.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classically compute Fourier coefficients of the Lévy noise and truncate to L terms.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure auxiliary qubit and, if needed, reverse the output state to recover the desired integral encoding.

speedup_claims.factor: quantum spectral implementation with O(L log L + log^2 T) quantum operations after classical preprocessing
speedup_claims.conditions: for stochastic integrals over Lévy noise with bounded Fourier-coefficient ratio C
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not give an explicit qubit count; it reports operation counts and a postselection success bound. No hardware experiment is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(T log T) resources for classical Fourier-coefficient computation plus O(L log L + log^2 T) quantum operations

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Algorithm 5.1 uses O(T log T) classical preprocessing and O(L log L + log^2 T) quantum operations for the stochastic-integral encoding.
limiting_factors: Postselection success probability depends on Fourier-coefficient ratio
Classical computation of Fourier coefficients is required

notes: No hardware experiment is reported; this is a theoretical algorithmic result.
The paper gives operation counts rather than an explicit qubit count for Algorithm 5.1, so num_qubits is left as a qualitative statement.
The paper presents a theoretical spectral method for Lévy-process integrals, not an empirical benchmark.

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo algorithm using coherent analog encodings of fractional Brownian motion to estimate inner products / time averages, including applications to variance swaps and anomalous diffusion.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo with coherent analog encodings and amplitude estimation

hyperparameters.f: test function encoded as a quantum state
hyperparameters.Bmax: upper bound on path norm for postselected variant

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Use coherent analog encoding of fBM trajectories; encode test function f(t) as a quantum state and estimate overlaps/amplitudes.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[<f(t)|BH(t)>/||BH(t)||] or E[<f(t)|BH(t)>] for fractional Brownian motion trajectories.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Amplitude estimation; optional postselection on bounded-norm paths.

problem_instance.description: Monte Carlo estimation over fractional Brownian motion trajectories; includes variance-swap pricing and anomalous-diffusion statistics as applications.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare coherent analog encoding of fBM; optionally postselect on bounded-norm trajectories; encode f(t) as a quantum state.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare the fBM coherent analog encoding and the function state |f⟩; compute norms and conditional rotations.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude-estimation output interpreted as the desired expectation value; in applications, used to price variance swaps or compute diffusion statistics.

classical_baselines.method_name: standard quantum mean estimation with classical simulation oracle

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic in ϵ over classical Monte Carlo, plus polylog(T) dependence
speedup_claims.conditions: for coherent analog encodings of fBM; especially for H > 1/2
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the result is incomparable to standard quantum mean estimation because the analog simulator introduces additional ϵ-dependent error terms.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: standard quantum mean estimation with classical simulation oracle
speedup_claims.conditions: when using the fBM simulator as the oracle
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly calls this incomparable because the ϵ-scaling is worse than standard quantum mean estimation.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: eO(L + log T) qubits and eO(polylog(T)/epsilon^(1+1/2H)) gates.
limiting_factors: Amplitude estimation requires coherent oracle calls

notes: No hardware experiment is reported; this is a theoretical algorithmic result.
The paper states the runtime as eO((L + polylog(T) + G)/(ϵ||f||)) gates and simplifies it to eO(polylog(T)/ϵ^(1+1/2H)) in Theorem 6.3.
The paper explicitly states the quantum Monte Carlo method is asymptotically faster than classical Monte Carlo in T, but this is a theoretical claim only.

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo algorithm using coherent analog encodings to estimate expectations over fractional Brownian motion trajectories, including inner products and postselected variants.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo with coherent analog encodings for fBM

key_results: Estimates E[<f(t)|BH(t)>/||BH(t)||] with gate complexity eO(polylog(T)/epsilon^(1+1/2H))
Uses eO(L + log T) qubits with L = O(1/epsilon^(1/2H))
Classical Monte Carlo is eO(T/epsilon^2); standard quantum Monte Carlo with compiled classical oracle would be eO(T/epsilon)

experiments.description: Variance swap pricing application using fractional Brownian motion volatility and quantum Monte Carlo.

algorithm.variant: Variance swap pricing via coherent analog encoding of fBM volatility

key_results: Pricing scales as O(polylog(T) epsilon^-c) with c = 1 + 1/(2H), where 3/2 < c < 2 for H in (0,1]
Uses the fBM simulator and quantum mean estimation
The paper notes the option has a closed-form solution in the unpostselected case, so this is not a white-box speedup
